constraints: Do not run new hypothesis tests; reconcile and report existing results.
Every claim must trace to a named upstream artifact.
State the duplication conclusion in terms of the complexity metrics actually computed, not a restated QC percentage.
Label any sub-threshold gene as exploratory wherever it appears.
State the sample_01 handling decision and its consequence for group sizes.
steps.description: Assemble a decision-ready summary integrating T1S1 (QC and confounding checks), T1S2/T1S3 (primary DE and sensitivity to sample_01) and T2S1 (pathway signal). acceptance_criteria: A headline gene table with per-gene robustness annotation across the 12-sample and 11-sample analyses.
A limitations paragraph covering duplication, sample_01, QC-condition confounding, genes tested, and 6-vs-6 power.
Pathway statements restricted to enrichments not explained by rRNA/MT composition.
Sub-threshold candidates, if presented, explicitly labelled exploratory.

plan.title: Heart total-RNA treated vs control DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single gene-level Salmon count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 human heart samples) plus a 2-column metadata table encoding an unpaired 6-treated vs 6-control design, one batch, rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs. The question is a two-group differential expression question, so the backbone is a negative-binomial test on raw counts (DESeq2), preceded by a QC step that addresses the two documented hazards and followed by pathway interpretation. Two caveats drive the design. First, duplication above 60 percent: for rRNA-depleted total RNA without UMIs, duplication is expected and largely reflects depth on a transcriptome dominated by a few abundant and structural transcripts. It is not evidence of a corrupted library, and reads must not be deduplicated for count-based DE; only a count matrix is delivered anyway, so no dedup is possible or wanted. What the plan must do is check library complexity directly from the matrix (fraction of counts in the top 10/50/100 genes, genes needed to reach 50 percent of counts, residual rRNA/MT fraction) and test whether that complexity is confounded with condition, which is the failure mode duplication would actually cause. Second, sample_01 is roughly 4x below median depth. That is a depth problem, not automatic grounds for exclusion: DESeq2 size factors and the NB model handle unequal depth, but a shallow library detects fewer genes and can drive Cook's outlier calls. So T1S2 runs the primary DE on all 12 samples and T1S3 re-runs the identical contrast without sample_01, judging robustness by log2FC concordance rather than by significance counts, since dropping one sample also drops power. A third total-RNA issue is that residual rRNA and mitochondrial content varies with depletion efficiency and can distort size factors, so T1S1 quantifies it per sample and T1S2 reports whether size factors move when the dominant structural features are excluded. T2S1 runs pre-ranked GSEA on the full ranked statistic rather than an over-representation test on a thresholded list, because a 6-vs-6 contrast may yield too few threshold-crossing genes; gene sets come from the staged human hallmark, GO and canonical-pathway GMTs (msigdbr is not installed, so sets are read from files). T3S1 reconciles everything into a decision-ready summary that states the power reality of 6 vs 6 explicitly. One known unknown from the profile: the record does not say whether the Salmon gene-level counts carry a length or abundance correction. Raw estimated counts are the correct DESeq2 input; T1S1 tests integrality and reports it, and T1S2 branches on that finding rather than assuming.

Collapse redundant GO terms by leading-edge overlap before reporting a count of significant processes.
Set and record a random seed - fgsea permutation p-values are stochastic.
acceptance_criteria: Per-collection enrichment tables with NES, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value and leading-edge genes.
Gene identifier mapping rate to HGNC symbols reported.
Redundant GO terms collapsed before any count of significant processes is reported.
Hallmark stability check between the T1S3 and T1S2 rankings reported.
Any absent gene-set collection named explicitly rather than silently skipped.
caveats: GSEA on a 6-vs-6 contrast inherits that contrast's noise; a significant NES with a small, weakly-ranked leading edge is exploratory.

Enrichment of ribosomal, mitochondrial or structural-RNA-heavy sets may reflect residual rRNA-depletion efficiency differences flagged in T1S1 rather than biology - cross-check against the T1S1 per-sample rRNA/MT fractions before interpreting.
Hallmark, GO and canonical-pathway collections overlap; a process appearing in all three is one finding, not three.

steps.name: Integrated result summary with QC caveats
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to which genes differ between treated and control, given the duplication flag, the low-depth sample_01, and n=6 per group?
steps.description: Assemble a decision-ready summary integrating T1S1 (QC and confounding checks), T1S2/T1S3 (primary DE and sensitivity to sample_01) and T2S1 (pathway signal). Produce: (1) a headline table of significant genes from the carried-forward analysis with shrunken log2FC, padj, baseMean, and a per-gene robustness annotation indicating significance with and without sample_01 and any Cook's outlier flag; (2) a short statement of the treatment effect at pathway level, naming only enrichments not attributable to rRNA/MT composition per the T2S1 cross-check; (3) an explicit limitations paragraph stating the duplication finding as actually measured (library complexity from the count matrix), the depth status of sample_01 and how it was handled, whether QC metrics were confounded with condition, the number of genes tested out of 12,000, and the power reality of a 6-vs-6 unpaired design - large consistent effects detectable, modest ones not, so the list is a lower bound; (4) specific follow-ups that would resolve residual ambiguity (qPCR confirmation of top genes, re-sequencing sample_01, a larger or paired cohort). If the DE analysis returned few or no FDR-significant genes, say so plainly and present the strongest sub-threshold candidates labelled exploratory rather than reframing them as findings.
steps.context: Final synthesis. Inputs are the artifacts of T1S1, T1S2, T1S3 and T2S1. No new statistical modelling. The user's question is QC-aware, so the report must answer the duplication concern directly rather than only listing genes.
constraints: Do not run new hypothesis tests; reconcile and report existing results.
Every claim must trace to a named upstream artifact.
State the duplication conclusion in terms of the complexity metrics actually computed, not a restated QC percentage.
Label any sub-threshold gene as exploratory wherever it appears.
State the sample_01 handling decision and its consequence for group sizes.
acceptance_criteria: A headline gene table with per-gene robustness annotation across the 12-sample and 11-sample analyses.
A limitations paragraph covering duplication, sample_01, QC-condition confounding, genes tested, and 6-vs-6 power.
Pathway statements restricted to enrichments not explained by rRNA/MT composition.
Sub-threshold candidates, if presented, explicitly labelled exploratory.
caveats: Resist narrative pressure to produce a mechanism: with one factor, no time course and n=6, the honest output is a ranked gene list plus a pathway-level direction.
If T1S1 found QC metrics confounded with condition, that caveat must lead the limitations paragraph.
